answer.evidence: The main body is the pair of upright arcade cabinets in rows 0-34, a 30px wide block drawn face-on. Rows 0-4 are a marquee strip with a gradient and no front-edge line or eave shadow, so it is a vertical face. Row 5 is dark. Rows 6-19 are the screen bezel and screen. Rows 20-22 are a thin gray control strip with buttons, and rows 26-34 are the coin-door panel. No band, ellipse, roof or visible contents reads as a horizontal top surface on the cabinets, and no side face is drawn. The object is not a container with an opening. Only the small stools at rows 36-46 have ellipse cushion tops, and they are separate minor parts, not the main body.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's tile density is decent: 16 visible tones per tile against 17-20 for the stall and well, and 0% near-flat coverage. The structure is shallower than the references. Each cabinet reads as a flat body with a screen, a marquee and a button panel, and each material has only about 3 lightness steps (light, mid, dark) against 5-6 on the stall and well. The dark edge pixels are 100% near-neutral, so the outline is a uniform black/grey line around each cabinet and stool. That is the 'sticker' look. The stall, hedge and well use tinted dark-material edges (0-33% neutral). The surfaces have little grain, speckle or per-element highlighting beyond the screen glow, so the texture is limited. The piece is clean and readable, but a careful artist would not put it next to the stall and well without it looking flatter and more outlined.
